name: Vivek H. Rajpara
subrole: Agentic systems · LLM tooling · Payment infrastructure in Go
tagline: My agents take production work from raw evidence to a verified fix. I also build the Go payment systems they work on, which at Yuno connect merchants to 55+ processors.
location: Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India · IST with EU overlap · Remote
summary: I'm an AI-native backend engineer. My day job is owning payment-processor connectors at Yuno, a payment orchestration platform. These are Go microservices that handle authorization, tokenization, 3DS, webhooks and reconciliation for 55+ processors, wallets and fraud providers.

Agents changed how I work. I designed a suite of about 20 Claude Code skills that takes a production ticket from Jira, Slack and Datadog evidence to a root cause, a failing test, a fix, a staging-verified PR and a written evidence report, with every message to a person drafted for my approval first. That suite is how I authored 350+ PRs, reviewed 700+ and closed 470+ tickets in one year.

In 2026 my team of three won Yuno's Agents Hackathon with the Feature ETA Agent, which turns a feature request into a delivery date with P50/P80/P95 confidence. The dates are computed by code, never typed by the model. Each of us was awarded 5,000 ESOPs.
Outside work I build Nexus, a multi-agent research platform for markets. Its rule: no idea is trusted until it beats a random control.

ai_systems.title: On-call agent suite
ai_systems.text: About 20 Claude Code skills chained into one cycle: ticket diagnosis, payment and webhook forensics, alert triage, connector fixes with TDD, staging verification, PR review, release approval and deploy monitoring. Each skill pulls its own evidence from Jira, Slack, Datadog, the database and code.
ai_systems.metric: 350+ PRs · 700+ reviews · 470+ tickets in a year

ai_systems.title: Hands-off E2E payment bot
ai_systems.text: Creates a payment through the public API, follows the provider redirect in headless Chrome, and does whatever the sandbox page asks: approve, pick a bank, or type the 3DS OTP inside an iframe. It then waits for the callback, polls to a final status and collects Datadog evidence.
ai_systems.metric: removes the manual browser step from payment QA

ai_systems.title: Deploy-monitor agent
ai_systems.text: Spots a version change and compares old against new: error categories, provider latency p50/p95/p99, 2xx/4xx/5xx, resource use and decline mix, all measured against the same window last week. It keeps watching the canary and only raises anomalies that clear a calibrated bar.
ai_systems.metric: watches every 20 min while rolling, hourly for 12 h after

ai_systems.title: Evidence-first agent design
ai_systems.text: My agents never report state from memory. A verify-first rule makes them check every claim live before stating it, and a post gate re-reads the Slack thread or ticket right before replying so they never re-ask a settled question. Merges and production deploys always wait for a human.
ai_systems.metric: no outward message without one human approval

cases.title: First-poll race on a synchronous card processor
cases.symptom: The gateway acknowledged sales, then answered the first status poll with "request not found". Our adapter declined while the processor captured the money.
cases.fix: Moved the pending-code rule into one shared set for all five poll steps, added an unmapped-code warning, and documented the exhaustion path and its trade-off.

cases.title: Recurring charges failing at a gateway
cases.symptom: Merchant-initiated renewals were declined because the off-session and network-transaction-ID rules only applied to subscriptions.
cases.fix: Extended the merchant-initiated predicate to every stored-credential flow and normalized the network-transaction-ID format.

cases.title: Webhook 5XX storm
cases.symptom: A webhook endpoint returned 500 on events it should ignore, so the processor retried for days and flooded the alerts.
cases.fix: Changed the ignorable-error path to a 204 ack and added a monitor that tells provider retries apart from real failures.

featured.name: Nexus
featured.title: A multi-agent research platform for markets
featured.text: 24 agent modules (scanner, signal generator, a risk guardian with veto power, bull/bear debate, trade explainer, journal, retrainer) on a LangGraph state graph. Around them sit FastAPI services, Redis, Kafka, TimescaleDB, MLflow and Optuna experiment tracking, XGBoost models and a Next.js dashboard. It trades on paper only.
featured.point: The part I'm proudest of is the research gauntlet: walk-forward splits, permutation tests and random-entry controls. It has rejected most of the strategy variants it has tested, including many that looked great in a plain backtest. I trust that more than any single backtest.

projects.name: go-idempotency-middleware
projects.text: Go stdlib-only HTTP idempotency-key middleware: a retried POST never executes twice. Concurrent duplicates get 409, key reuse with a different body gets 422, and the record store is bounded and race-clean. Comes with a black-box conformance tester.

hackathon.name: Feature ETA Agent
hackathon.pitch: Give it a feature request. Get a delivery date you can defend.
hackathon.problem: Before, a feature request ended with a date somebody typed. Nobody wrote down which teams and services it touched, the date had no assumptions behind it, and priority got argued again in every meeting.

pillars.title: The model reads
pillars.text: It quotes the ticket, finds the teams and services, maps dependencies, proposes sizes and asks at most five questions. It is never allowed to type a date.

pillars.title: The code calculates
pillars.text: Python engines turn PERT effort estimates into a schedule, run 2,000 Monte Carlo simulations to get P50/P80/P95 dates, find the critical path and score priority with RICE and WSJF. 42 checks run at every step.

pillars.title: People decide
pillars.text: Team leads accept or adjust, security signs off, and nothing is written to Jira or Slack without a human approval. Every plan is versioned and re-planned when something changes.
